intro: Dallas rewards visitors with world-class museums, serious barbecue and a lively downtown core. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: DART light rail covers downtown and many suburbs; best for commuters.
DART buses reach most places but are slow and infrequent off-peak.
Tap a contactless card or phone on DART readers; you pay the cheapest valid fare.
Taxis hail at stands and hotels; Uber and Lyft both work widely.
A car is the simplest way around; rush hour on I-35 and US-75 is brutal.
Downtown is walkable; bikes and scooters suit short hops, not sprawl.

dealey-plaza.name: Dealey Plaza
dealey-plaza.tip: Come early morning to see the grassy knoll and the X marks on Elm Street without crowds.

smu.tip: Walk the tree-lined boulevard and see the George W. Bush Presidential Center next door.

wingstreet.name: WingStreet

itz.price_text: Buffet plus game credits · check on the day

klyde-warren.name: Klyde Warren Park
klyde-warren.tip: A park built over the freeway between Downtown and Uptown; food trucks often park here at lunch.

dallas-arts-district.name: Dallas Arts District walk
dallas-arts-district.price_text: Free to walk · museums charge entry
dallas-arts-district.tip: Walk between the Dallas Museum of Art, the Nasher and the Crow Museum in one loop.

dallas-museum-art.name: Dallas Museum of Art
dallas-museum-art.price_text: Free general admission · special shows ticketed
dallas-museum-art.hours: Closed Monday · Tue–Sun daytime · check on the day
dallas-museum-art.tip: General entry is free; go for the free collection and check what special exhibition is on.

deep-ellum.name: Deep Ellum street walk
deep-ellum.hours: Best in the evening; bars open late
deep-ellum.tip: Murals, live music and barbecue; walk Main Street and look up at the wall art.

bishop-arts.name: Bishop Arts District
bishop-arts.price_text: Free to walk · pay per shop and cafe
bishop-arts.hours: Shops daytime; restaurants into the evening
bishop-arts.tip: Independent shops and cafes a short drive from Downtown; good for a relaxed half-day.

katy-trail.name: Katy Trail
katy-trail.tip: A shaded walking and cycling path through Uptown; rent a bike or just stroll a section.

peggy-suelen.name: Peggy Sue BBQ
peggy-suelen.price_text: ≈ USD 15–25 per person · check on the day
peggy-suelen.hours: Usually lunch and dinner daily · check on the day
peggy-suelen.tip: Classic Dallas barbecue near SMU; try the brisket plate.

stays.why: Walk to the Sixth Floor Museum, the Arts District and the convention center. DART rail lines meet here.
Restaurants and bars along McKinney Avenue, a short walk or trolley ride from downtown.
Live music, murals and late-night food. Lively at night, quieter by day.
Good-value hotels and a short drive to Uptown and downtown. Cedar Springs nightlife nearby.

food: Try Texas BBQ brisket and ribs; popular spots sell out by late afternoon, so go early or check on the day.
Tex-Mex is the local staple: fajitas, enchiladas and queso. Expect USD 12–25 a plate.
Breakfast tacos are a cheap Dallas ritual, often USD 3–5 each. Grab them from a taqueria or food truck.
Deep Ellum and Uptown have the densest restaurant rows. Book ahead for weekend dinner.
Tipping is expected: about 20% at sit-down restaurants and bars.
more_time: Add a half-day at the Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden, or the Perot Museum of Nature and Science for families.
Sports fans can swap a museum for a Cowboys or Mavericks game; check the schedule and ticket prices on the day.
Drive 30–40 minutes to Fort Worth for the Stockyards and its twice-daily cattle drive.
